Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Item 2 — Example: Finding the Median of a Dataset With an Odd Number of Values

Example Prompt:
[MATH: 95,\: 97,\: 99,\: 100,\: 101,\: 102,\: 104,\: 106,\: 108]

What is the median of the data values given above?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
The median is the middle value of a data set when the values are arranged in order from smallest to greatest.

To find the median, we first check that the data is in increasing order. In this case, it is already sorted:

[MATH: 95,\: 97,\: 99,\: 100,\: 101,\: 102,\: 104,\: 106,\: 108]

There are [MATH: 9] data values, which is an odd number. When the number of values is odd, the median is the value in the exact middle. That means we take the [MATH: 5]th value:

[MATH: 95,\: 97,\: 99,\: 100,\: \bbox[3pt,Gainsboro]{101},\: 102,\: 104,\: 106,\: 108]

Therefore, the median is [MATH: 101.]
